 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. In this story One of Week 7's most anticipated matchups unfolds on prime time as the Seattle Seahawks host the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday Night Football. While this game could have playoff implications, the biggest storyline centers around Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III's return to the Pacific Northwest to face his old team.
 Here's how the " Football 301 " podcast crew of Nate Tice and Matt Harmon sees this matchup playing out on Sunday.
 What to expect from Walker's return to Seattle 
 After an offseason that saw the Seahawks make a controversial decision to let Super Bowl MVP Walker walk in free agency, the Chiefs pounced, handing the explosive playmaker a backfield all to himself. Walker has swiftly become the "identity force" in Kansas City, revitalizing a Chiefs run game that had long struggled for consistency and big plays.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement During the Football 301 podcast, the emotional and strategic angles were not lost. "Sometimes the Revenge Game stuff is nonsense," Harmon said. "I kind of think he wants to come in here and have a big game against the team that pretty much just said, 'Thanks for winning us that Super Bowl… we're going to give your money to Rashid Shaheed'"
 Despite Kansas City coaches' comments to the contrary, Walker's workload has been heavy. He has 106 carries for an NFL-leading 665 yards and six touchdowns, along with two receiving TDs.
 Good on good: elite offense vs. elite defense 
 On paper, the game promises classic strength-on-strength. Kansas City's offense, first in both yards per play and success rate, goes up against a Seahawks defense ranked first in both explosive plays and yards per play allowed.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes appears to be in peak form, making big throws, improvising under pressure and enabling a receiving corps that, while not loaded with stars, features a blend of vertical threats and physical role players. Tight end Travis Kelce's impact remains high both as a receiver and as a blocker, giving the Chiefs versatility to attack Seattle multiple ways.
 Seattle's defense, led by creative play-caller Mike Macdonald, enjoys a deep line rotation and formidable secondary. Their ability to limit explosive plays and force offenses into inefficiency has been a hallmark, setting up an intriguing chess match between two of the NFL's brightest minds in Macdonald and Chiefs head coach Andy Reid.
 How will Seattle respond? 
 For the Seahawks, the question is whether their defense can keep Walker in check and slow a surging Kansas City attack. "If you can get this Seahawks defense in any ways… sometimes running backs in the passing game [are the answer]," the podcast highlighted.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement On the flip side, the crew noted the Seahawks' offense is hampered by a struggling run game and a lack of complementary weapons for Jaxon Smith-Njigba. Defenses have heavily clouded and bracketed him, daring Seattle to win elsewhere. The Chiefs' defense, meanwhile, excels at bracketing top receivers and will likely try to take away JSN, forcing someone else to step up.
 QB Sam Darnold's struggles under pressure and against man coverage were cited as a vulnerability for Seattle — particularly with Chiefs defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo dialing up exotic blitzes.
 Prediction 
 Both analysts expect the game to tilt toward the Chiefs due to their offensive versatility and the Seahawks' challenges in finding secondary offensive contributors. If the Chiefs' offense is neutralized by the Seahawks' D, the Chiefs' defense still holds advantages against a one-dimensional Seattle attack. The recipe for Seattle to pull the upset would require new wrinkles from their offensive coaching staff — something there's little indication of so far.
